claims.claim: Google search has been personalized for everyone since December 4, 2009.
claims.episode_span: Google announced personalized search results for all users in December 2009
claims.supporting_quote: Since December 4, 2009, Google has been personalized for everyone. So when I had two friends this spring Google "BP," one of them got a set of links that was about investment opportunities in BP. The other one got information about the oil spill

claims.claim: Google reportedly used 57 different pieces of data (including location) to personalize a user's search results.
claims.episode_span: drawing on 57 signals including location and prior queries
claims.supporting_quote: As of 2011, one engineer had told Pariser that Google looked at 57 different pieces of data to personally tailor a user's search results

claims.claim: Pariser's BP example: one user searching "BP" got investment news while another got Deepwater Horizon oil-spill information.
claims.episode_span: When two people searched “BP” after the Gulf spill, one received investment analysis while the other received environmental criticism
claims.supporting_quote: He related an example in which one user searched Google for "BP" and got investment news about BP , while another searcher got information about the Deepwater Horizon oil spill

claims.claim: Eli Pariser coined the term filter bubble (circa 2010) and his 2011 book The Filter Bubble predicted intellectual isolation from algorithmic personalization.
claims.episode_span: Pariser’s 2011 book and TED talk brought the term “filter bubble” into wider use.
claims.supporting_quote: The term filter bubble was coined by internet activist Eli Pariser circa 2010. Pariser's book The Filter Bubble (2011) predicted that individualized personalization by algorithmic filtering would lead to intellectual isolation and social fragmentation.

claims.claim: The filter bubble idea was popularized by Pariser's TED talk in May 2011.
claims.episode_span: Pariser’s 2011 book and TED talk brought the term “filter bubble” into wider use.
claims.supporting_quote: Pariser's idea of the filter bubble was popularized after the TED talk in May 2011

claims.claim: Facebook announced its News Feed on September 6, 2006.
claims.episode_span: By 2006 Facebook’s News Feed and by 2009 Google’s personalized search results extended the same logic
claims.supporting_quote: On September 6, 2006, Facebook announced a new home page feature called "News Feed". The new layout created an alternative home page in which users saw a constantly updated list of their friends' Facebook activities.

claims.claim: Item-to-item collaborative filtering was invented and deployed by Amazon.com in 1998.
claims.episode_span: Collaborative filtering, first widely deployed by Amazon in 1998, used past clicks and purchases
claims.supporting_quote: Item-item collaborative filtering was invented and used by Amazon.com in 1998.
